convention.unit: 1 Blender unit = 1 metre. Positions in this file are WORLD coordinates (the game's X/Z and height Y); bakeLightmap.py converts them into the model's own frame with the asset's `placement`.
convention.lightmapValue: Scene-linear radiance a WHITE diffuse surface would show under the baked lights (light only, no albedo). Stored as Radiance .hdr.
convention.runtimeIntensity: Three.js divides irradiance by pi when it applies albedo, so lightMapIntensity = pi reproduces the bake's exposure exactly; scale from there when tuning against the game grade.
convention.candela: Light strengths are in the game's candela terms (the same units as VISUAL_STYLE.lighting.streetLightIntensity). A Cycles point light of P watts has radiant intensity P / (4 pi) in these units, measured by bake in Blender 5.2 (1000 W lit a white plane 2 m below to L = 6.32 = I / (pi d^2)).
convention.sky: The world colour is the game's hemisphere ambient: ambientSky * ambientIntensity / pi, so an open-sky white surface reads the same radiance the game's ambient light gives it.
convention.uv: TEXCOORD_1, named `Lightmap`, one atlas across the whole building. UV0 is untouched (the tiling metric UVs).
convention.denoise: Cycles ignores its denoise flag when baking, so both maps are denoised afterwards with the compositor's OpenImageDenoise node.

placement.source: WORLD_LOCATIONS dreams (front: north) + replaceDreamsFallback in src/world/createWorld.ts: position (x, 0, z), rotation.y = PI

building.excludeReason: The 96 brick-joint strips are hidden at runtime (applyDreamsModelPolicy) because drm-brick carries its own joints; they get a zeroed lightmap UV so the vertex layout stays uniform, and neither take atlas space nor cast.

ground.extentFrame: model frame: X across the frontage, Y toward the street (negative = in front of the shopfront), metres

tubes.from: VISUAL_STYLE.lighting.coldWhite. Each of the eight fascia tubes is a mesh light; candelaEach is the bake's own exposure choice (the game's tube glow is an emissive/bloom cheat with no photometric value).
